original_question: Can some or all groups of the following sorts be written as homomorphic images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups? This is Question 18 in(G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274(2015) 451–495). (a) Infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent. (b) For an infinite set X, the group of those permutations of X that move only finitely many elements. It is known that no group of permutations containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit can be written as an image of such an ultraproduct(ibid.).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.11 in the Kourovka Notebook's "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", which explicitly points back to Bergman's Question 18; the sharper original formulation is Question 18 in Section 4 of Bergman's paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient problem: homomorphic images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups, together with the two intended test cases and the nearby permutation-group obstruction from Corollary 14. It is especially close to the Kourovka restatement in Problem 21.11. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To make the setup fully stand-alone, the ultraproduct should be written explicitly as (prod_{n∈ω} G_n)/U with U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω; Lemma 10 is the result that reduces the general case to this countable-index formulation. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))

If you want the wording closest to Bergman's original Question 18, item (a) should be stated as the Burnside-group case: an infinite finitely generated Burnside group. Problem 21.11 in Kourovka restates this more expansively as infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))

The quantifier should be sharpened: Bergman's paper poses the two cases separately, while Kourovka 21.11 asks whether some or all groups of each listed type arise; your draft leaves that scope a bit loose. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

In item (b), the group should be named explicitly as the finitary symmetric group FSym(X), namely the permutations of an infinite set X with finite support. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))

The known negative fact about permutation groups is context rather than an extra assumption: Corollary 14 shows that any permutation group containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit cannot be such a homomorphic image. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))
refined_question: For each of the following two types of groups, determine whether some, all, or no members of that type can occur as homomorphic images of a nonprincipal countable ultraproduct of groups, that is, of an ultraproduct (prod_{n∈ω} G_n)/U with U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω: (i) infinite finitely generated Burnside groups (the original wording of Bergman's Question 18; in Kourovka 21.11 this appears as infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent); and (ii) the finitary symmetric group FSym(X) on an infinite set X, consisting of the permutations of X with finite support. In the second case, the question is to be read in light of Corollary 14, which already excludes permutation groups containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: By Lemma 10, this is equivalent to asking whether such groups can be realized as homomorphic images of ultraproducts (prod_{i∈I} G_i)/U over arbitrary index sets I, provided only that U is not countably complete. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))
justification: The draft is already close to the paper's target problem, but the paper-faithful sharpening is to make the ultraproduct notation explicit, identify the second group as FSym(X), and align the first case with Bergman's original Burnside-group wording while noting the Kourovka reformulation. Lemma 12 and Corollary 14 are the nearby results that explain why these examples are singled out: Lemma 12 gives a necessary condition for being such a homomorphic image, and Corollary 14 explains why the full symmetric group is ruled out while the finitary symmetric group remains the unresolved permutation-group case highlighted by Question 18 and Problem 21.11. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/pjm/2015/274-2/pjm-v274-n2-p08-s.pdf))
